title: Ab Urbe Condita, books 35-37 - 36
author: Livy
source: Translated by Claude from phi0914.phi00136.perseus-lat1, as held by the Perseus Digital Library.

passages.original: magnam partem agminis aut lassitudine subsistentis aut errore, ut qui sine ducibus per ignota itinera fugerent, dissipatos oppresserunt; nec praeter quingentos, qui circa regem fuerunt, ex toto exercitu quisquam effugit, etiam ex decem milibus militum, quos Polybio auctore traiecisse secum regem in Graeciam scripsimus, exiguus numerus: quid, si Antiati Valerio credamus sexaginta milia militum fuisse in regio exercitu scribenti, quadraginta inde milia cecidisse. supra quinque milia capta cum signis militaribus ducentis triginta?
passages.english: [but] it overwhelmed a large part of his column, scattered as they were, halting either from exhaustion or from losing their way, since they were fleeing without guides along unknown routes; and apart from the five hundred who were around the king, no one out of the whole army escaped, a tiny number even out of the ten thousand soldiers whom, on the authority of Polybius, we have written that the king brought across with him into Greece. What if we were to believe Valerius Antias, who writes that there were sixty thousand soldiers in the royal army, that forty thousand of them fell, [and that] over five thousand were captured, along with two hundred and thirty military standards?
passages.notes: The passage continues a sentence begun in the preceding context ("The Roman cavalry did not overtake the king himself at Elatia;"), hence the bracketed "[but] it". The punctuation of the final question is as printed: the full stop after "cecidisse" seems to belong inside the question, and it has been translated as one continuous question.
